_comment: Where each bundled artifact came from, so `gameversion.status()` can say
whether it still matches the installed game. Regenerate an entry's
`gameBuild` whenever you re-run its script against a new install.
A null `gameBuild` means the origin build is genuinely unknown, not that it
is current. `gameversion` reports that as 'unknown' rather than assuming a
match, because a wrong-but-plausible map is worse than an honest banner.

gamedata.json.gz.source: refs/palworld/.../Pal-LinuxServer.pak (numbers, plus DT_PalMonsterParameter.BestWorkSuitability/ZukanIndexSuffix/IgnoreCombi) + refs/Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en (display strings); refs/PalWorldSaveTools-main.zip supplies artwork paths and catalogue membership only
gamedata.json.gz.note: Display names and descriptions now come from the game's own L10N tables (scripts/l10n.py, scripts/gametext.py) and the numeric columns were verified against the server pak's DataTables 13,836/13,836 by scripts/verify-gamedata.py. The archive remains the source of icon paths and of which ids exist at all, so the entries the game does not name still carry its value -- build-gamedata.py prints that count per section as 'still from archive'. gameBuild is the client pak's build, which is where the strings come from. `bestWorkSuitability` is read directly from the server pak (753/753) because the reference archive does not carry it: it is the per-species half of the condenser mechanic, whose magnitude is in no data file — see task #74. MOVEMENT AND MOUNTS ADDED for backend/buildplanner.py. `movement` carries RideSprintSpeed/RunSpeed/WalkSpeed/SlowWalkSpeed/SwimSpeed/SwimDashSpeed/TransportSpeed/Stamina for all 753 forms, with the game's own -1 DROPPED rather than carried — it is a 'not applicable' sentinel on 60/52/105 species respectively and ranking it as a slow speed would bury them. `rideable` + `mountGearItem` come from DT_PartnerSkillParameter.RestrictionItems, 288 forms / 149 base species. THIS CORRECTS AGENTS.md, which said RestrictionItems 'does not settle' rideability and named Galeclaw as the counterexample: Galeclaw is NOT in RestrictionItems. Measured — 143 Essential_PalGear items, 126 named by some RestrictionItems, and the 17 named by none are EXACTLY the partner gear you hold or wear rather than ride (five gloves incl. Galeclaw's, three companion-summoning necklaces, two harnesses, a headband, a power converter). Every known non-mount checked is absent and every known mount present, so RestrictionItems IS the mount list. It still says nothing about MODE: whether a mount flies, swims or walks is in no file, and two further avenues checked while adding this changed nothing — the client pak has no BP_Pal_<species> blueprint, and the 213 per-species animation folders do not attribute it (Jetragon has no fly-named animation; everything has an Idle_Swim). Fastest RIDE is answerable; fastest FLYER is not.

effigies.json.gz.note: 396 positions and instance GUIDs, read from the always-loaded relic cell. Positions are static per build; a content update can move or add relics.

passive_effects.json.gz.note: The numeric effects of all 1,897 passives — effect type, signed percentage, target and invoke conditions. gamedata.json.gz carries only the English sentence ("Attack +5%"), which cannot be computed with. Verified against that prose: 1,754 of the 1,759 passives with a numeric description match exactly; four of the five exceptions are the archive failing to substitute its own {EffectValue1} placeholder, and the fifth (FullStomach_Down_1_BossDefeat) is an unresolved disagreement.

game_settings.json.gz.note: Pocketpair's own 347 tuning constants — damage rates, sanity and hunger thresholds, capture rates, base-camp ranges. Decoded from a Blueprint CDO rather than a DataTable, which is a capability nothing else here had. Self-verifying: the walk must terminate at the end of the export (41,416 of 41,420 bytes) AND reproduce CharacterMaxLevel=80 and CharacterMaxRank=5, two constants previously held from sources that could not be checked against the install. Run with --verify after a game update. Grew from 6.4 KB to 15.7 KB on 2026-08-07 when uassettable learned to decode MapProperty: WorkSuitabilityDefineDataMap now yields the per-work-type CraftSpeeds curves for the ten types that had been assumed to share the three stated ones — eight of them do not, and Handcraft reaches 5,400 at rank 10 against Mining's 1,000. The decode's own check is that the map's keys minus the pseudo-entry 'Anyone', plus the three standalone types, are exactly the 13 work suitabilities the species table ships.

boss_spawners.json.gz.note: 90 placed field bosses with species, LEVEL and world position — levels 11-79, 89 distinct species. The table has 159 rows; 69 are unused spawner slots and are not bosses. Positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 90/90 land on an occupied MainGrid_L0 cell at 25,600 units, with controls at 12,800 (22/90) and 51,200 (83/90) both worse, which is what makes it evidence. Contains no RAID_ ids and should not: raid bosses are altar-summoned, not world-placed.

pal_breeding.json.gz.source: tylercamp/palcalc precomputed table, layered with refs/PalWorldSaveTools-main.zip
pal_breeding.json.gz.note: 44,850 precomputed pairs plus the game's own combi/unique tables. Neither source is a pak, so there is no build id. Breeding results change only when Pals are added or the combi table is edited.

pal_db.json.gz.note: Per-Pal breeding attributes (rank, gender ratio) backing the planner. Same sources as pal_breeding.json.gz and regenerated by the same script.

worldobjects.json.gz.note: 59,396 objects across 13 categories: 27,408 ore, 13,752 Pal spawners, 9,923 chests, 3,503 fishing spots, 2,163 dungeon objects, 794 junk piles, 705 stat lotuses, 473 supply drop points, 220 NPCs/camps, 185 oil fields, 103 coins/pots, 99 field bosses, 68 skill and affection fruit. Grew from 51,921 after a coverage check over all 916 placeable actor classes in the pak found the ore, treasure and fishing patterns were too narrow — `Spawner_Treasure_*` and `SpawnerTreasureBox*` are different families one underscore apart, and matching only the second still returned a plausible-looking 8,386. Field bosses are the alpha Pals that drop Ancient Technology Points and carry a resolved `species` (97 of 99). Effigies stay excluded: they have their own bundle carrying the GUIDs saves key on. Tower bosses are NOT here — they are fast-travel points named '… Tower Entrance' (gamedata.fast_travel_kind). The most update-sensitive artifact here: terrain edits move these.

habitats.json.gz.note: 478 species with cells, LEVEL RANGE, spawn count, group weight and time/weather restriction. Replaces the name-table workaround (scripts/extract-pal-habitats.py), which inferred a rosterby intersecting a package name table with the species list -- 348 species, no levels, no rates, and explicit that a hit meant "references this species" rather than "spawns here". 32 forms the workaround found are absent here because DT_PalWildSpawner contains ZERO PREDATOR_ entries: predators are placed by another mechanism. 30 of those 32 have their base species covered and the other 2 are _Quest variants, so nothing a player can look up got worse; build-habitats.py refuses if that stops being true. weight is relative WITHIN one spawner group only.

icons/.note: 1,409 icons (pals, items, elements, npcs) into public/icons/, filenames preserved so the `icon` paths already recorded in gamedata.json.gz resolve directly. A game update adding Pals or items adds icons; existing ones rarely change. Underlying artwork is Pocketpair's — see docs/LICENSING.md.

work_assign.json.gz.note: 158 structures with the work suitability each needs, the MINIMUM rank a Pal must have, worker cap, sanity drain per tick and species restrictions. 271 rows because a structure can have several work slots — a farm plot needs Seeding, Watering and Collection, so reading only slot 0 answers a third of the question. This mapping was twice documented as absent from every game file (backend/optimise.py and backend/basesupply.py); it was in a sibling of the table those checked. Verified two ways: every work id resolves against the bundled list of 13, and the structures ABSENT from the table are exactly the ones no Pal is assigned to — on refworld, 44 of 63 base-placed kinds resolve and the 19 that do not are chests, beds, palbox, spa, walls and food boxes. WorkerMaxNum is 0 on 178 of 271 rows including quarries that plainly take workers, so it is NOT a capacity of zero; workerMaxIsUnset travels beside it.

basecamp.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak DT_BaseCampLevelData / DT_BaseCampWorkerSickDataTable / DT_BaseCampWorkerEventDataTable; condition NAMES and descriptions from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UI_Common_Text_Common
basecamp.json.gz.note: 35 base levels with the worker cap (1-30) and bases-per-guild cap (up to 4), 8 illnesses with their real work-speed, move-speed and satiety penalties plus the hourly palbox cure chance, and 11 worker events with the sanity each triggers at. THE LEVEL TABLE IS A DEFAULT, NOT A BOUND, and that is measured: a real server in use runs 5 bases per guild and 25 workers, over the table in one direction and under it in the other. BaseCampWorkerMaxNum, BaseCampMaxNumInGuild and BaseCampMaxNum are all PalWorldSettings.ini keys, so the INI is the only authority and gamedata.server_limit() reads it; None means not known, never unlimited and never 'use the game's value'. Base level is not in the save at all (BaseCampSaveData carries id, name, state, transform, area_range, group and the owning palbox, and the palbox carries no level either), so the per-level table currently has no caller. Illness detail: DisturbingElement is -50%/-50% at only 3%/hr palbox cure; Cold is -5% at 20%/hr — so 'sick' can stop being a flag. The sanity thresholds matter separately: a worker takes short breaks at 85 and has stopped being useful well before main.LOW_SANITY's 50, which comes from FriendshipPoint_AutoIncrementRequireSanity and measures trust gain rather than misbehaviour. Read verification: the table's top worker cap of 30 must be >= the 25-slot worker container observed on the live world. Debug_DisplayName is Pocketpair's internal Japanese label, flagged debugNameIsInternal so nothing renders it. Condition display names come from the client pak because the server table carries only an internal SickType and the event table's debugName is Japanese. `Cold` displays as "Sick" — the id and the player-facing name genuinely disagree, which is why they are looked up rather than humanised. Without the client pak the bundle still builds and `nameIsInternal` is true.

economy.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_ItemRecipeDataTable, DT_PalDropItem, DT_ItemLotteryDataTable, DT_ItemShopCreateData, DT_PalShopCreateData, DT_StatusEffectFood, DT_MapObjectItemProductDataTable, DT_TechnologyRecipeUnlock_Common, DT_PalStaticItemIDRedirectData)
economy.json.gz.note: 1,414 recipe rows over 1,399 products, 890 species with drop tables, 500 loot fields (8,777 entries with real WeightInSlot rates), 38 item shops, 8 Pal shops, 53 foods, 16 production structures, 588 technology unlock rows and 29 item redirects. Closes tasks #35 and #36, which were filed against the CLIENT pak and were impossible there — unversioned properties give only a name table. RECIPES ARE A LIST PER PRODUCT. The first version kept one and reported 1,399, discarding fifteen rows including TWELVE OF THE THIRTEEN ways to get a Paldium Fragment (one per kind of Pal Sphere dismantled) and the choice between Coal and Charcoal for Carbon Fibre. Right for 'how do I make X', wrong for 'where does X come from', which is what backend/itemsource.py answers. THE TECHNOLOGY JOIN NEEDS A CASE-FOLD and the check is what found it: two of the 588 rows spell a recipe differently from the recipe table (Bow_triple/Bow_Triple, Sakurasaurus/SakuraSaurus). An FName compares case-insensitively; a dict does not, so an exact join silently loses two technologies. Every recipe a technology names must resolve to a recipe ROW (not a product — reading them as products would resolve for the handful whose row name matches and look like a working join) and every prerequisite technology must exist, or the write is refused. DT_PalStaticItemIDRedirectData IS NOT A RENAME MAP, however exactly it reads like one. All 29 rows point an accessory's _2 and _3 tiers at its _1, and all 58 source ids already resolve to DISTINCT names — the game calls Accessory_AT_2 'Attack Pendant +1'. Wiring it into gamedata lookups, which is what the task proposed, would replace 58 correct names with 29 wrong ones and undo the tier distinction the L10N join exists to get right. It is bundled as data with its meaning stated and NO lookup consults it. Pal-shop rosters carried stringified dicts ("{'Key': 'SheepBall'}") until this regeneration: FName cells decode as {"Key": ...} and str() on that serialises perfectly while resolving to nothing. Invisible because nothing read them. WorkableAttribute is carried by every recipe row and is 0 on ALL of them, so it is deliberately not bundled — which bench crafts what still has no source and must not be inferred from this table. Drops are level-BANDED: the Level column holds only 0, 10, 20 ... 80, so a row covers 'level 30-39'. Interpolating would be inventing. BOSS_ variants have their own drop tables and the prefix is NOT stripped, unlike pal() naming. Verification is asymmetric on purpose: every ITEM id must resolve or the write is refused (the catalogue is complete at 2,466, so a miss means the projection drifted), while unknown SPECIES are an advisory — 32 of 890 are absent and all are real (_BossRush arena variants, quest NPCs, plain humans), matching the known incompleteness palcheck already documents. One food row (BaconEggs_53) does not decode and is dropped with a report rather than guessed at; 53 of 54 are clean. EACH RECIPE ALSO CARRIES craftExpRate, denyRecipeChain AND A DERIVED isConversion, added for backend/crafting.py's recursive tree. SIXTEEN PRODUCTS SIT IN A CYCLE — a Pal Sphere is crafted from Paldium Fragment and dismantles back into it, and the four Pal Soul sizes trade both up and down — and no column says which direction is production. The test is a CONJUNCTION and either half alone is wrong: the structural half (the product is transitively required by its own materials) is true in BOTH directions and cannot pick one, while CraftExpRate == 0 is true of every conversion AND of seventeen ordinary crafts (Money, Baked Berries, every gym head band). Together they name exactly 16 rows, and the acceptance criterion is not that those rows look like dismantles: it is that removing them leaves a graph with ZERO cycles, asserted in verify() and again in test_crafting.py against this shipped file. What falls out is right rather than merely consistent — all four Pal Soul sizes end up with no production recipe at all, which is the game. denyRecipeChain is 94 rows naming 373 targets and turns out to be a weapon's own higher TIERS, not anything cyclic; nothing consults it yet.

spawns.json.gz.note: 8,253 spawn points with verified world positions and 420 rosters giving species, level range, count range, weight, time and weather. SUPERSEDES the name-table intersection in scripts/extract-pal-habitats.py, which reaches 348 species and can only ever claim 'this blueprint references this species' rather than 'spawns here at this rate'. This reaches 482 with real numbers. Positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 8,253/8,253 land on an occupied MainGrid_L0 cell at 25,600 units, with controls at 12,800 (3,288) and 51,200 (7,791) both worse — both controls doing worse is what makes it evidence. The extractor refuses if any position falls off the grid, if a control ever matches as well, or if species coverage drops below the 348 baseline. TWO DISCREPANCIES RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: 72 FieldBoss placements here against 90 in boss_spawners.json.gz (DT_BossSpawnerLoactionData) — different tables, neither known to supersede the other; and 8 of 372 spawner names match no roster row and are kept with an empty one, since a spawn point whose contents are unknown is still a spawn point. DT_PaldexDistributionData was the obvious source for Paldeck habitats and is NOT usable: its dayTimeLocations/nightTimeLocations are a natively-serialised struct array uassettable cannot walk, with no independent check available for 365 species.

moves.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_WazaDataTable, DT_WazaMasterLevel, DT_WazaMasterTamago, DT_PalCombiUnique, DT_PalMonsterParameter for tribes)
moves.json.gz.note: 384 moves with element, category, power, cooldown and range; 712 species with level-up move lists; 283 with inheritable egg moves; 258 unique breeding combinations across 333 tribes. Egg moves are the reason people breed past the species chart and nothing in the dashboard has surfaced them. Move ids are stripped of the EPalWazaID:: prefix once, at this boundary, matching what the API speaks everywhere; charedit re-attaches it only on write. DT_PalCombiUnique is keyed on TRIBES, not species — a tribe covers every variant, which is why 258 rows describe every special pairing. Resolved through DT_PalMonsterParameter.Tribe rather than guessed from the id. GENDER IS LOAD-BEARING ON EXACTLY ONE PAIR: 256 of 258 rows say 'either', and the two that do not are CatMage x FoxMage, giving FoxMage_Dark for Male+Female and CatMage_Fire for Female+Male. A table keyed on an unordered pair can hold only one of those. PALCALC COMPARISON, reported not applied (see #64): of the ungendered rows, 251 agree and 0 disagree. 1,106 'missing' are BOSS_/PREDATOR_ variants palcalc does not carry at all (it holds 305 base species). The only real gap is the gendered pair, where palcalc reports FoxMage_Dark and loses CatMage_Fire. So the breeding planner's third-party foundation is sound on everything it can structurally represent. Verification is asymmetric as in extract-economy.py: every WazaID must resolve in DT_WazaDataTable or the write is refused, while 29 unknown species (_BossRush arena variants, _otomo partner forms) are an advisory.

progression.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_PlayerStatusRankMasterDataTable, DT_GainStatusPointsItem, DT_WorldMapAreaData, DT_PalQuestLocationData, DT_DungeonSpawnAreaDataTable, DT_DungeonLevelDataTable); relic line NAMES/descriptions and MAJOR BOSS ENCOUNTER NAMES from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UI_Common_Text_Common (BUILDUP_PLAYER_STATUS_NN, BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_*)
progression.json.gz.note: 13 relic types across 279 ranks with their effect rates and respec costs; 11 stat elixirs; 123 named regions; 166 quest world positions; 23 dungeon areas with 15 layouts. Unblocks two half-built features: the map has shown all 396 effigies and which a player found since the layer shipped without ever saying what finding them achieved (#61), and `areasFound` is an opaque flag map that 123 region ids turn into '47 of 123' (#47). EffectRate is 0.0 at rank 1 for EVERY relic type — the game's baseline meaning 'unlocked, no bonus yet', not a decode failure. Reading it as missing data would be wrong in the first place anyone looks. Region MsgIDs (REGION_Desert_1) are carried UNRESOLVED: they are keys into the localisation tables, and humanising them here would create a second source of truth against those. Quest positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 166/166 on occupied cells at 25,600, controls at 12,800 (70) and 51,200 (151) both worse. 166 points is a much smaller sample than the 8,253 in spawns.json.gz, so a coincidence is cheaper and the controls matter more, not less — the extractor refuses if either matches as well. 23 dungeon areas carry only 15 layout rows between them; the rest have none in DT_DungeonLevelDataTable and keep an empty list. Relic line names are joined POSITIONALLY (the L10N keys are indexed 00-12, not keyed by RelicType) and the join is anchored on four distinctive pairs -- CapturePower/'Capture Power', StaminaReduction/'Endurance', SphereHoming/'Sphere Tracking', MoveSpeed/'Movement Speed'. extract-progression.py REFUSES the build if any drift, because a mislabelled stat line is unverifiable once shipped. ALSO 14 major boss encounter names, which is what TowerBossDefeatFlag is keyed on: a save writes BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_GrassBoss and the game calls it 'Rayne Syndicate Tower', so humanising the key gave 'Grass Boss'. THE FLAG MAP HOLDS MORE THAN TOWERS and `kind` records which is which -- 8 towers, 3 World Tree mid-bosses, 2 endgame encounters and 1 ARENA (BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_KingWhaleRoom, 'Eternal Sea'), so a denominator over the whole table would count a room. The 8 towers are checked against the eight '... Tower Entrance' fast-travel points, which come from the world cells rather than from this table -- two unrelated files agreeing is what makes it evidence, and the extractor REFUSES if they stop agreeing. Two encounters carry the game's own '？？？' placeholder: that is Pocketpair withholding a spoiler, not a decode failure, and it travels as `hidden` rather than being repaired or humanised into a name the game refused to give.

raidbosses.json.gz.note: 11 summon rows carrying 11 boss forms, levels 35-80, with summon items, rewards and egg weights. CONFIRMS an earlier refusal rather than overturning it: boss_spawners.json.gz holds 90 PLACED field bosses and zero RAID_ ids, which is correct because raid bosses are altar-summoned and a table of locations has nothing to say about them. NO POSITIONS and none must be invented — a map marker would be the BP_LevelObject_TowerLockBarrier mistake. Count FORMS not rows: a row's InfoList can hold more than one boss, and row-counting is what briefly turned 90 field bosses into 159. Advisory: 6 of 11 forms are `_2` difficulty variants (Bellanoir Libero and friends) that the bundled character tables carry no entry for — predicted before the check ran, since AGENTS.md already records what the suffix means. REWARDS SHIPPED EMPTY FOR A WHOLE RELEASE and the fix is the lesson: _items read `ItemId`/`StaticItemId`, the spellings the drop and lottery tables use, while this table's column is `ItemName` -- and an FName at that, so str() on it would have given "{'Key': 'AncientParts2'}" even had the name matched. Every boss came out with an empty reward list, no error, and 'this raid drops nothing' reads as an ordinary answer. Now 11 of 11 carry rewards over 50 distinct items, every one resolving in the catalogue, and the extractor REFUSES if not one boss has a reward -- a raid the game does not reward is not a thing, so an empty result across the board is a reader fault by definition. `Rate` is carried because it is a real per-item chance here: these are independent rolls on one success rather than shares of a slot, unlike a lottery weight. EGG WEIGHTS ARE NOT READ AND SAY SO. EggPalIDAndWeight is a MapProperty and uassettable decodes none; the old code iterated it as a list -- over the characters of the string '<MapProperty 98B>' -- and produced [] for every boss, which reads as 'this raid drops no eggs'. eggWeightsRead: false now travels instead. The row key IS the summon item: PalSummon_NightLady resolves in the catalogue as "Bellanoir's Slab", so 'what starts this raid' is a lookup rather than an inference, and the rewards chain -- clearing Bellanoir Libero drops the Ultra slab.

invaders.json.gz.note: 44 base-raid attacker groups across 143 entries, 76 reward tables, 48 friendly visitor types, cancel costs 500-40,000. gradeMeaningKnown is FALSE and travels in the payload: InvadeGradeMin/Max bound a raid to a 'grade' and nothing establishes what a grade is in save terms (base level, guild level and player level are all plausible). This is a reference table, NOT a per-base forecast. The join check runs attacker -> reward, not the reverse. An attacker with no reward is a raid that drops nothing; a reward with no attacker is an unused row, and the game ships 32 of those — rewards exist for the mainland biomes (Basic, Desert, Forest, Volcano) while DT_PalInvader carries only the island groups. Measured 44 of 44 attackers rewarded. The first version checked the harmless direction and would have blocked the extraction over the game having spare data. A few DT_PalInvader columns do not decode and are skipped; the fields read here come through cleanly.

worldpresets.json.gz.note: The game's own four difficulty presets (Easy, Normal, Hard, Hardcore) with 43 settings each, plus 4 world-mode preset rows. A CROSS-CHECK on backend/presets.py's hand-made presets rather than an automatic replacement: DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini is authoritative for WHICH settings exist and says nothing about what a difficulty changes, so these two together are two sources where there was one. If the existing presets already match, that is worth recording. The game's own typo is preserved in the source column name — it is `Diffculty`, not `Difficulty`. Only the output key is normalised, so a grep for the correct spelling finds nothing in the pak. Values uassettable could not walk come back as `<WorldMode 9B>` strings and are excluded rather than shipped as settings.

npcs.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (MainGrid streaming-cell ACTORS + DT_UniqueNPC); display names from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UniqueNPCText_Common
npcs.json.gz.note: 438 placed NPCs with role, level, respawn time and verified world position, of which 404 carry an identity. THIS IS THE UNVERSIONED-PROPERTY WALL COMING DOWN FOR WORLD ACTORS. upackage.py documents that a placed actor's properties cannot be decoded, and that is true of the CLIENT pak and false of the SERVER pak -- the same correction uassettable.py records for DataTables, never pointed at world cells until now. A MainGrid_*.umap in Pal-LinuxServer.pak carries IntProperty/StructProperty/NameProperty in its name table, so a spawner actor's tagged properties walk exactly like a DataTable row's: UniqueName -> a DT_UniqueNPC row -> 'Black Marketeer', plus HumanName, Level and RespawnTime. This is what makes 141 anonymous BP_MonoNPCSpawner placements nameable; worldobjects.json.gz's 220-point 'NPCs & camps' layer could only ever say someone stood there. THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS WEAKER THAN read_table's AND SAYS SO. An actor export cannot prove alignment by ending exactly at the buffer end -- 32-43 bytes of component instancing data follow the property terminator. What replaces it is RESOLUTION: every identity must be a DT_UniqueNPC row or a known character, because a drifted tag walk does not produce 400 valid foreign keys. The extractor refuses above a 5% miss rate; the 3 that do miss (BOSS_Female_Soldier, BOSS_Scientist_LaserRifle, BOSS_VikingElite) are the character tables' documented incompleteness -- AGENTS.md names Scientist_LaserRifle specifically -- and are an advisory, the same asymmetry extract-economy.py applies to species. Positions verified against the cell grid: 438/438 at 25,600 with controls at 12,800 (72) and 51,200 (437) both worse. 4 placements were DROPPED for failing that check, all BP_OilrigNPCSpawner_Mono -- read_position's byte scan finding the wrong triple of doubles. Checked rather than waved through: those four sit 60,000 units from the nearest oil rig in worldobjects.json.gz, and oil rigs themselves pass the same grid test 185/185, so 'the grid does not cover the sea' is ruled out. Dropping beats refusing the other 438; the extractor refuses if the drop rate exceeds 5%. THE ROLE SPLIT IS A NAME RULE, not a game column -- DT_UniqueNPC carries appearance and talk-flow only, and TalkBPClass is a flavour label with 58 of 216 rows set to None. It fails safe like gamedata.fast_travel_kind: an unrecognised id is a plain `npc`, which is what all 220 were before. roleFromName travels in the API payload. SEPARATELY MEASURED AND NOT BUNDLED: the wandering merchants have NO location anywhere. DT_RandomIncidentNPC_DarkTrader (x4) and _MarchantwithPAL (x3) name the NPC and its level and carry SpawnLocation (0,0), while 149 of the 195 incident rows across those tables DO carry real coordinates -- so the merchants are specifically the ones the game does not place. A naive grid check passes all 195 at EVERY cell size, because (0,0) is a real occupied cell; the controls are what caught it.

guild.json.gz.note: Four guild ranks and eight permissions, named by the game. Exists because the save's guild_chest_allowed_roles and role_permissions carry bare enum indices and 'role 2' helps nobody. THE RANK JOIN IS DERIVED AND ANCHORED FOUR WAYS; THE PERMISSION JOIN IS NOT MADE AT ALL, and the asymmetry is the whole point. Ranks: four names against observed indices 2/3/4 rules out a 0-based enum outright, index 1 is the one absent from every role_permissions list (the Guild Master needs no explicit grants), permission counts fall monotonically with the index (5, 2, 0), and guild_chest_allowed_roles [2,3] excluding 4 reads as 'Guests may not use the chest', which is the game's own default. Four independent checks agreeing is the standard extract-progression.py sets for its positional relic join, and the extractor REFUSES if any stops holding. Permissions: eight names against indices 0-7 agree on the COUNT and say nothing about the ORDER -- the L10N keys are alphabetical, which is a property of the text table rather than of the enum, and the C++ enum is not in the pak. So the bundle ships a LIST with permissionOrderKnown:false and no index-keyed map; a caller indexing into it would assert an order nothing supports, and the failure mode is a screen telling an operator a rank can kick players when it cannot.

settings_help.json.gz.source: docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/{configuration,arguments,commands} (per-key descriptions, Pocketpair's own documentation) + refs/Pal-Windows.pak DT_UI_Common_Text WORLDSSETTING_* (labels and enum value names)
settings_help.json.gz.note: THE ONLY BUNDLE WITH A NON-PAK SOURCE, and the fetch is a build step -- the container never reaches the network. 93 of the INI's 119 keys carry an official description, 50 carry the game's own label, and 19 carry nothing at all rather than a guess; the extractor prints that list and refuses below 60 documented keys, which is what a changed page layout looks like. The UI_ALIASES map (game UI row -> INI key) is hand-written and each entry is confirmed by the pak string and the doc row describing the same thing; run with --show-aliases to re-check. Six of the 19 are PvP keys the pvp page names only inside prose recipes, which is not a per-key description. A handful of `note` fields are this dashboard's own measurements and are tagged noteSource=dashboard so they are never mistaken for Pocketpair's.

lab_research.json.gz.note: The Pal Lab research tree: 168 nodes, 9 roots, across the 9 work types that have research. Each carries its prerequisite, up to four material costs, a RequiredWorkAmount in work UNITS (never a duration — how long depends on assigned Pals, which no file states), and a typed effect using the same EPalPassiveSkillEffectType vocabulary as passive_effects.json.gz. The build refuses if any RequiredResearchId resolves to no row, because a broken edge renders as a node nobody can reach and reads as a game rule rather than a bug; all material ids are checked against the item catalogue and all resolve. Ten rows carry EPalPassiveSkillEffectType::no — the game's own 'grants no rate' — and are normalised to null so a client never renders 'no +0%'. Research is guild-wide and permanent, and the save records progress in GuildExtraSaveDataMap[].Lab.RawData.research_info.
